column1: # slug|impact,uniqueness,significance,experience,depth|category overrides or -|individual rationale
national-museum-of-korea|9.1,9.3,9.4,9.3,9.6|-|Exceptional national collection with substantial depth, but not as globally irreplaceable as the National Palace Museum's imperial objects.
changdeokgung-palace|9.3,9.4,9.6,9.4,9.2|-|Outstanding Joseon palace with preserved gardens, but visitor and historical scope remain below the Forbidden City ensemble.
bulguksa-temple|9.2,9.4,9.6,9.3,8.9|-|Silla architectural landmark with important Buddhist heritage; compact temple visitation differs from Angkor's vast complexes.
haeinsa-temple|9.1,9.6,9.7,9.0,8.7|-|Tripitaka Koreana gives exceptional textual heritage significance, not necessarily unrestricted visitor depth in its living monastery.
seokguram-grotto|9.0,9.4,9.5,8.9,7.7|-|Exceptional Buddhist sculptural chamber but short contained visit has far less depth than museum collections or large temple parks.
huwon-secret-garden|8.8,9.0,8.9,8.9,8.1|-|Unique royal garden tour within Changdeokgung; avoid inheriting all parent palace significance and discovery.
jongmyo-shrine|8.8,9.3,9.7,8.8,8.0|-|Confucian royal ritual significance is high; site experience and breadth are narrower than palaces or comprehensive heritage areas.
suwon-hwaseong-fortress|9.1,9.3,9.4,9.2,9.0|-|Important surviving fortification system, but the visitor scale is less globally singular than the Great Wall.
hahoe-folk-village|9.0,9.3,9.4,9.2,8.9|-|Living traditional settlement and heritage architecture, but globally comparable preserved villages exist.
yangdong-folk-village|8.9,9.2,9.3,9.1,8.7|-|Notable historic Korean clan settlement; distinguish wider village heritage from global reference towns.
jeju-island|9.2,9.2,9.1,9.3,9.6|-|Entire volcanic island offers varied experiences, but individual volcanic attractions carry their own scientific distinctiveness.
hallasan-national-park|9.2,9.3,9.0,9.1,9.4|-|Strong volcanic summit and high-altitude habitat, although comparable alpine national parks exist worldwide.
seoraksan-national-park|9.3,9.3,9.0,9.3,9.4|-|Outstanding granite peaks and valleys, but not every dimension merits rare worldwide benchmark status.
gyeongbokgung-palace|9.0,9.3,9.5,9.1,8.9|-|Major royal palace complex with deep history; avoid near-unique scale when compared with Forbidden City and Changdeokgung.
daereungwon-ancient-tombs|8.7,9.0,9.3,9.0,8.5|-|Important Silla royal burial mounds but interpretive depth and impact are below entire Gyeongju Historic Areas.
manjanggul-lava-tube|8.9,9.3,8.9,8.9,8.0|-|Excellent lava tube geology but a single cavern should not inherit Jeju Island's multi-site ecological depth.
ulleungdo-island|8.9,9.2,8.6,9.1,9.1|-|Remote volcanic island scenery and distinctive ecology, but not every experience dimension is globally elite.
geomunoreum-volcanic-cone|8.7,9.0,9.0,8.8,8.1|-|Important Jeju volcanic geology, yet focused volcanic cone trail is less substantial than the whole UNESCO volcanic ensemble.
jeonju-hanok-village|8.7,8.9,8.7,9.0,8.7|-|Attractive concentrated traditional streets with commercialized tourism; cultural atmosphere does not equate to top historic towns.
suncheon-bay-wetland-reserve|8.9,9.0,9.0,9.1,8.6|-|Outstanding tidal wetland and bird habitats, with visitor depth and global rarity below the largest protected ecosystems.
namhansanseong-fortress|8.8,9.0,9.1,8.9,8.6|-|Significant mountain fortress with hiking, but less monumental visitor distinctiveness than globally top defenses.
buseoksa-temple|9.0,9.2,9.2,9.0,8.5|-|Important wooden architecture and Buddhist landscape, but compact temple tour is narrower than grand temple precincts.
tongdosa-temple|9.0,9.2,9.3,9.1,8.7|-|Major Buddhist monastery with meaningful grounds, while global historical singularity is below top pilgrimage complexes.

gyeongju-historic-areas|9.5,9.6,9.8,9.5,9.8|-|Retain UNESCO historic ensemble spanning numerous archaeological monuments and 1000-year Silla urban culture; broad area is materially deeper than its individual tombs and temples. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/976

seongsan-ilchulbong|9.1,9.5,9.1,9.2,8.2|-|Keep exceptional UNESCO-listed oceanic tuff cone and global volcanological distinctiveness, while reducing exploration depth to the focused summit trail rather than all of Jeju Island. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1264/

bangucheon-stream-petroglyphs|8.9,9.5,9.6,8.5,8.5|history=9.8,culture=9.6|The 2025 UNESCO-listed Bangucheon property encompasses two major rock-engraving panels across a three-kilometre stream landscape documenting long prehistoric maritime and ritual art; this is a coherent historic ensemble, not a single etching. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1740

bangudae-petroglyphs|8.7,9.2,9.5,8.4,7.8|history=9.7,culture=9.5|The Bangudae rock art panel is archaeologically important for whale and animal imagery, but it is one component of the wider Bangucheon UNESCO property and usually a comparatively short viewpoint visit. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1740

bongjeongsa-temple|8.6,9.0,9.3,8.8,8.3|architecture=9.3,history=9.5|Bongjeongsa is a Sansa UNESCO mountain-monastery component with valuable historic wooden Buddhist architecture; the single monastery has narrower interpretive depth than entire Gyeongju Historic Areas. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

daeheungsa-temple|8.6,9.0,9.3,8.9,8.7|history=9.4,architecture=9.2|Daeheungsa's woodland Buddhist monastery forms part of the UNESCO Sansa serial inscription, with important monastic tradition but lower unique global monument density than Angkor or large historical capitals. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

beopjusa-temple|8.7,9.1,9.4,8.8,8.3|history=9.6,architecture=9.4|Beopjusa is an important Buddhist monastery in the UNESCO Sansa group, with monumental wooden pagoda and sacred landscape, while a single temple still has a concentrated sightseeing footprint. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

byeongsan-seowon-academy|8.5,9.1,9.3,8.7,8.1|history=9.4,architecture=9.3|Byeongsan Seowon contributes to UNESCO Korean Neo-Confucian academy heritage, combining education buildings and landscaped principles; its heritage significance exceeds the scale of one courtyard visit. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

dosan-seowon-academy|8.5,9.0,9.2,8.7,8.4|history=9.3|Dosan academy is a major Neo-Confucian educational site and UNESCO Seowon component, but lacks the combined depth and rare scale of the full serial academy group. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

gongsanseong-fortress|8.7,9.0,9.3,8.9,8.7|history=9.5,architecture=9.3|Gongsanseong is a substantial Baekje fortress and capital-defense ensemble inside the UNESCO Baekje Historic Areas; fortress walls and landscape allow meaningful exploration without duplicating the full heritage property. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

jisan-dong-tumuli-goryeong|8.5,9.0,9.3,8.5,8.2|history=9.4|The Jisan-dong tomb cluster is a significant archaeological element of UNESCO Gaya Tumuli with extensive elite burials, but mound visitation and museum interpretation have more modest immediate tourist impact. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

gochang-dolmen-site|8.6,9.1,9.5,8.3,8.1|history=9.6,culture=9.4|Gochang dolmens represent a major prehistoric megalithic group in Korea's UNESCO serial dolmen property; significant archaeology should not be equated with rich multi-room visitor experience. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

seonamsa-temple|8.5,9.0,9.3,8.8,8.5|architecture=9.3,history=9.4|Seonamsa is a historic forest monastery within the UNESCO Sansa group, notable for Korean Buddhist religious continuity and architecture, with site-local depth distinct from a whole national sacred landscape. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

tomb-of-king-muryeong|8.5,9.2,9.4,8.5,7.8|history=9.5,culture=9.3|The excavated King Muryeong tomb is central to the UNESCO Baekje Historic Areas and provides rare royal burial evidence, but its singular chamber has lower on-site exploration depth than entire fortress and museum ensembles. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

jirisan-national-park|9.2,9.1,9.2,9.2,9.4|-|Jirisan was South Korea's first national park and spans an expansive mountain range with significant ecological and sacred-mountain traditions, providing much more than one summit viewpoint but less rare globally than the highest volcanic or glacial parks. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?menuSn=351&vcontsId=93604

hallyeohaesang-national-park|9.0,9.0,8.8,9.1,9.5|-|Korea's first marine national park spans six separate coastal districts and many islands, supporting varied multi-day sea scenery and hikes, unlike a single harbor overlook or beach. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=110638

jinju-fortress|8.8,9.0,9.2,9.0,8.6|-|Jinju Fortress preserves major Imjin War battlefield history and accessible walls, pavilion and museum, giving deeper regional military history than a single monument but lower global military singularity than the Great Wall. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?menuSn=351&vcontsId=75199

gyeongju-national-museum|9.1,9.3,9.4,9.2,9.4|-|Gyeongju National Museum holds extensive Silla royal and Buddhist collections including national treasures and thousands of historical objects, with materially more museum depth than ordinary small local collections. Source: https://www.museum.go.kr/ENG/contents/E0608000000.do

mireuksa-temple-site|8.8,9.4,9.5,8.8,8.6|-|The excavated Mireuksa Temple Site forms part of UNESCO Baekje Historic Areas and preserves the enormous early Korean Buddhist pagoda, which justifies strong historical importance while its fragmentary ruins limit visitor immersion. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1477

donggung-palace-and-wolji-pond|8.8,9.0,9.0,9.3,8.0|-|Donggung and Wolji preserve the picturesque pond and secondary Silla palace grounds in Gyeongju, celebrated for night reflections, but a contained heritage pond visit should not inherit the city's entire ancient capital depth. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=94404

jeju-haenyeo-museum|8.5,8.8,9.3,8.7,8.1|-|Jeju Haenyeo Museum interprets the island's UNESCO-recognized traditional women-diver culture through exhibits; intangible traditions merit significance, but this museum is distinct from experiencing the entire living coastal tradition. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=103315

hwaeomsa-temple|8.6,9.0,9.2,8.8,8.5|-|Hwaeomsa's extensive historic Buddhist precinct sits below Jirisan, with stone lanterns and multiple halls; a more substantial temple visit than a roadside shrine but smaller than Gyeongju's complete historic district. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hwaeomsa

baengnokdam-crater-lake|8.9,9.2,8.0,8.6,7.9|-|Baengnokdam is the dramatic summit crater lake of Hallasan volcano within UNESCO Jeju volcanic heritage; strenuous summit hiking and weather make the lake a focused destination rather than the entire park. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1264

daeseongdong-tombs|8.4,9.0,9.4,8.1,7.7|-|Daeseong-dong tombs in Gimhae represent significant elite Gaya burials and archaeology; a component cemetery of UNESCO Gaya Tumuli has strong history but modest on-site variety. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1666

gotjawal-forest|8.8,9.3,8.9,8.9,8.7|-|Jeju Gotjawal lava forests support unusual humid microhabitats and biodiversity over porous volcanic rock, with worthwhile interpretation walks; a forest ecosystem rather than a single photographed tree.

beomeosa-temple|8.5,8.9,9.1,8.7,8.4|-|Beomeosa is a venerable Busan mountain monastery with historic gates and halls beside Geumjeongsan; cultural importance is high domestically but its area is smaller than Asia's great temple cities.

independence-hall-of-korea|8.8,9.2,9.4,9.1,9.4|-|Cheonan's Independence Hall covers the Korean independence struggle through extensive permanent exhibitions and large memorial grounds, providing more history and museum depth than a compact monument. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_Hall_of_Korea

naganeupseong-folk-village|8.7,9.1,8.8,9.0,9.0|-|Naganeupseong is a remarkably intact inhabited Joseon-era walled village with thatched homes and fortress walk, offering more heritage immersion than a reconstructed stage-set settlement.

marisan-tumuli-haman|8.4,9.1,9.4,8.2,8.3|-|Haman Marisan royal mounds form an important Gaya Confederacy cemetery in the UNESCO serial inscription, meaningful archaeology but a short mound-walk compared with an entire ancient capital. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1666

songgwangsa-temple|8.5,8.9,9.2,8.8,8.8|-|Songgwangsa is among Korea's major Seon Buddhist monastic centers, with forest approaches and historic temple halls; living religious heritage provides depth without global Angkor-scale architecture. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songgwangsa

woljeongsa-temple|8.5,8.7,9.0,9.1,8.8|-|Woljeongsa features an early stone pagoda and celebrated fir-tree approach within Odaesan, giving an unusually pleasant forest-temple experience; one monastery remains narrower than its national park. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woljeongsa

juwangsan-national-park|8.9,9.0,8.5,9.0,9.1|-|Juwangsan protects sandstone cliffs, forested gorges and pond landscapes with multiple hikes; a substantive mountain park, although its geology is less globally unprecedented than Jeju lava caves. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/infoHtmlView.do?menuSn=177&vcontsId=145437

oksan-seowon-academy|8.5,9.0,9.3,8.5,8.0|-|Oksan Seowon is a heritage Neo-Confucian academy with a quiet riverside setting and scholarly architecture; its UNESCO Seowon membership reflects educational history while the physical visit is concentrated. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1498

ulsanbawi-rock|9.0,9.3,8.1,9.2,8.3|-|Ulsanbawi is Seoraksan's striking jagged granite ridge climbed by steep stairs, an iconic mountain hike with outsized visual impact but not its parent park's full ecological significance.

busosanseong-fortress|8.6,9.0,9.3,8.8,8.7|-|Busosanseong fortifications preserve the Baekje capital defense landscape above Buyeo, offering wooded rampart hikes and multiple sites; important as part of the UNESCO Baekje Historic Areas. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1477

jusangjeolli-cliff|8.7,9.2,8.5,8.8,7.4|-|Jeju's Daepo Jusangjeolli cliffs expose strong polygonal basalt columns carved by the surf, a vivid geological viewpoint but less discovery depth than a complete volcanic island. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1264

seongeup-folk-village|8.4,8.6,8.5,8.7,8.4|-|Seongeup presents Jeju's traditional thatched architecture and village culture within an inhabited heritage settlement; cultural continuity is meaningful while tourist commercialization limits a flawless experience.

jeju-olle-trail|8.8,8.8,7.8,9.1,9.5|-|The island-wide Jeju Olle footpath links many coastal and inland walking stages, yielding major multiday exploration depth; it is a route rather than one singular world-monument. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeju_Olle_Trail

seoul-city-wall|8.7,9.0,9.0,9.0,9.2|-|Seoul's Hanyangdoseong city walls span ridge and urban neighborhoods along former Joseon capital defenses; broad connected hikes merit genuine depth while not equal to the Great Wall's size. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul_City_Wall

un-memorial-cemetery-busan|8.4,9.0,9.2,8.5,8.3|-|The United Nations Memorial Cemetery in Busan is an internationally significant Korean War burial and commemoration site, contemplative rather than a broad war-history museum. Source: https://www.unmck.or.kr/eng/main.do

wanggung-ri-archaeological-site|8.5,9.0,9.2,8.4,8.1|-|Wanggung-ri contains significant Baekje-era palace and pagoda archaeology at Iksan; outstanding heritage context but mostly fragmentary ruins compared with an intact palace. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1477

hyangiram-hermitage|8.6,9.0,8.4,9.0,8.1|-|Hyangiram is a small Buddhist hermitage perched on rugged Yeosu seaside cliffs, highly memorable for its coastal views and religious setting though not a vast ancient monastery.

jeju-april-third-peace-park|8.7,9.1,9.6,8.9,8.6|-|Jeju April 3 Peace Park documents mass violence, trauma and reconciliation through dedicated memorials and exhibitions, carrying national historic gravity beyond an ordinary landscaped garden.

jeongnimsa-temple-site|8.4,9.1,9.4,8.6,7.9|-|Jeongnimsa's surviving Baekje stone pagoda is a defining relic of Buyeo, though this focused temple archaeology site should not inherit the full UNESCO Baekje area's exploration breadth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1477

cheonjeon-ri-petroglyphs|8.5,9.4,9.5,8.0,7.5|-|Cheonjeon-ri engravings record prehistoric and historic rock art within the UNESCO Bangucheon landscape; rare cultural evidence outweighs the short and sometimes difficult visual observation. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1740

sosu-seowon-academy|8.5,9.1,9.5,8.7,8.3|-|Sosu Seowon helped establish private Neo-Confucian academies in Joseon Korea, offering influential educational heritage and historic wood buildings within one compact precinct. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1498

sanbangsan-mountain|8.8,8.9,8.0,8.9,7.9|-|Sanbangsan is a conspicuous steep volcanic dome rising from southern Jeju near coast paths and religious sites; outstanding island scenery without a full park's hiking scope.

yongmeori-coast|8.8,9.1,8.3,8.8,7.7|-|Yongmeori Coast reveals layered volcanic tuffs sculpted along the sea, striking and educational but tide and weather limit access and the walk covers only a small stretch.

may-18-national-cemetery|8.6,9.1,9.6,8.7,8.3|-|Gwangju's May 18 National Cemetery memorializes the 1980 democracy uprising with major Korean historical significance; solemn burial grounds are not intended as immersive entertainment.

oedo-botania|8.6,9.1,7.8,9.1,8.3|-|Oedo Botania is a landscaped private marine garden island with terraces, sculptures and sea panoramas, distinctive as an excursion while not a natural pristine biodiversity reserve.

bijarim-forest|8.5,9.1,8.5,9.0,8.6|-|Bijarim preserves a major concentration of ancient Japanese nutmeg trees on Jeju with tranquil interpretive trails, ecologically interesting but less vast than full national parks.

magoksa-temple|8.5,8.9,9.2,8.8,8.4|-|Magoksa is a historic Korean forest monastery in the UNESCO Sansa group, with decorated halls and a stream approach; noteworthy living heritage but limited standalone site depth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1562

cheomseongdae-observatory|8.5,9.3,9.6,8.1,6.6|-|Cheomseongdae's ancient stone astronomical tower in Gyeongju is rare early scientific architecture, internationally important but viewed largely as a single small exterior monument.

ganghwa-dolmen-sites|8.5,9.2,9.4,8.3,8.2|-|Ganghwa's prehistoric stone tombs form part of the UNESCO Korean dolmen serial property, significant megalithic evidence spread across sites rather than one expansive museum. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/977

soswaewon-garden|8.3,9.0,9.1,8.8,7.9|-|Soswaewon exemplifies Joseon literati landscape-garden design with pavilions and forest streams, culturally important but a concentrated garden visit rather than a full palace landscape.

daecheongbong-peak|8.9,8.8,7.7,8.9,8.3|-|Daecheongbong is Seoraksan's highest summit, reached by demanding hikes through varied ridge terrain; high scenic payoff but less cultural singularity than the surrounding park's heritage sites.
boriam-hermitage|8.6,8.9,8.3,8.9,7.8|-|Boriam is a compact mountain cliff Buddhist hermitage above the South Sea, offering remarkable coastal and island panoramas without major temple-complex depth.

gamcheon-culture-village|8.6,8.7,8.1,9.1,8.5|-|Gamcheon is a colorful stepped residential village and public-art maze in Busan, rewarding to walk but the modern mural redevelopment has less ancient authenticity than preserved Joseon settlements. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamcheon_Culture_Village

gwangjang-market|8.5,8.5,8.3,9.2,8.4|-|Gwangjang Market is a dense, longstanding Seoul food and textile market offering highly engaging culinary culture, though one commercial market is less globally irreplaceable than major heritage palaces. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwangjang_Market

haedong-yonggungsa-temple|8.8,8.8,8.1,9.0,8.1|-|Haedong Yonggungsa's temple terraces occupy a spectacular rocky Busan shoreline, notable especially for scenic setting; its present complex differs from Korea's most historically influential mountain monasteries. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haedong_Yonggungsa

cheongju-early-printing-museum|8.6,9.2,9.7,8.6,8.4|-|The Cheongju Early Printing Museum interprets Jikji and early movable-metal-type printing, globally consequential technology history with somewhat more focused on-site depth than a national history collection. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheongju_Early_Printing_Museum

third-infiltration-tunnel|8.4,9.1,9.2,8.5,7.6|-|The DMZ Third Tunnel was dug beneath the Korean border and is experienced through restricted subterranean visits, unusually direct Cold War military evidence but a short tightly managed site.

udo-island|8.7,8.6,7.6,9.0,8.8|-|Udo near Jeju offers coastal cycling, beaches, basalt geology and small village stops over an island outing, attractive but less singular than Jeju's full volcanic World Heritage property. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udo_(Jeju_Province)

boseong-green-tea-fields|8.5,8.6,7.9,9.0,8.2|-|Boseong's sculpted green tea rows create striking terraced hill scenery with tea culture visits, but cultivated farmland is less geologically rare than natural mountain landscapes.

dora-observatory|8.2,8.7,8.9,8.6,7.3|-|Dora Observatory provides a carefully controlled view across the Korean DMZ into North Korea, meaningful geopolitical experience but brief viewing-platform exploration. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dora_Observatory

naejangsan-national-park|8.7,8.5,7.9,9.1,8.9|-|Naejangsan is famed for dense autumn maple foliage, gorges and temple trails, offering a rich seasonal hiking park rather than a globally rare geological formation.

seonunsa-temple|8.4,8.6,8.8,8.8,8.3|-|Seonunsa's Buddhist halls in a forested mountain valley have strong historic traditions and seasonal camellias, with less monumental scale than Bulguksa's global Silla architectural legacy. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seonunsa

war-memorial-of-korea|8.8,8.9,9.3,9.2,9.3|-|Seoul's War Memorial holds extensive military-history exhibits, large equipment displays and Korean War commemoration, deeper and more educational than single DMZ lookouts. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_Memorial_of_Korea

baekje-cultural-land|8.4,8.2,8.1,9.0,8.7|-|Baekje Cultural Land reconstructs royal architecture for interpretation and family visits; engaging site scale should not be mistaken for surviving authentic Baekje archaeological monuments. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baekje_Cultural_Land

geumjeongsanseong-fortress|8.5,8.8,8.6,8.7,9.1|-|Geumjeongsanseong's long mountain-wall remains and gates above Busan make an extensive historic hiking experience, but dispersed ruined walls are less singular than fully preserved citadels.

jeju-folk-village|8.2,8.3,8.1,8.8,8.7|-|The Jeju Folk Village museum demonstrates historic island homes, tools and crafts in an assembled complex, strong educational variety but different from an inhabited traditional settlement.

jeju-stone-park|8.4,8.7,8.3,8.9,8.8|-|Jeju Stone Park combines volcanic-stone displays, folk myths and outdoor sculpture landscapes, a broad interpretive visit whose uniqueness comes from island geology and culture. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeju_Stone_Park

hwanseongul-cave|8.8,9.2,8.4,9.0,8.3|-|Hwanseongul is a massive limestone cave with guided interior walking routes, stalactite formations and active subterranean stream, substantial cave depth below the world's most exceptional underground systems. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hwanseon_Cave

seonjeongneung-royal-tombs|8.5,8.8,9.1,8.5,8.4|-|Seonjeongneung is a pair of Joseon royal burial precincts within UNESCO Royal Tombs of the Joseon Dynasty, important funerary landscape but not the breadth of the entire serial property. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1319

suncheon-bay-national-garden|8.7,8.7,7.9,9.2,9.2|-|Suncheon Bay National Garden includes broad themed plantings, sculpture zones and walking routes beside the wetland region; beautifully visitable but a designed garden is distinct from the protected tidal ecosystem. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suncheon_Bay_National_Garden

ssanggyesa-temple|8.2,8.6,8.8,8.8,8.3|-|Ssanggyesa Temple on Jirisan is known for early Korean tea history and forest approach, rewarding Buddhist heritage while not nationally as architecturally singular as Haeinsa or Bulguksa. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ssanggyesa

korean-dmz-imjingak|8.4,8.7,9.1,8.8,8.7|-|Imjingak is a large Korean War and division memorial park with bridges, rail relics and exhibits, meaningful complex but lower direct military rarity than a true infiltration tunnel.

guinsa-temple|8.7,9.1,8.4,8.9,9.0|-|Guinsa's vast stepped mountain monastery and modern Cheontae Buddhist halls create dramatic spatial architecture, high visitor depth despite limited ancient-monument historical significance. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinsa
